metadata.data_source: KPMG Datacenter Intelligence Unit — Compiled from public filings, operator disclosures, and market research (2024–2026)
metadata.notes: Capacity figures represent commissioned IT load unless stated otherwise. Tenant lists are indicative based on publicly known anchor clients.

datacenters.name: Yotta NM1 — Hiranandani Fortune City
datacenters.cooling_type: Chilled Water with Hot/Cold Aisle Containment
datacenters.notable_facts: India's first hyperscale data center park. Houses over 7,200 racks across 5 buildings with an eventual buildout target of 200 MW.

datacenters.name: STT GDC Mumbai DC1 — Airoli
datacenters.notable_facts: Part of STT GDC's INR 5,000 crore MoU with Maharashtra for AI-ready datacenter expansion at Palava campus targeting 400 MW.

datacenters.name: Equinix MB1 — Chandivali
datacenters.cooling_type: Precision Air Cooling with Hot Aisle Containment
datacenters.notable_facts: Equinix's first IBX datacenter in India. Acquired additional 1.38 acres in Chandivali for INR 155 crore to expand Mumbai presence.

datacenters.name: Equinix CN1 — Chennai
datacenters.notable_facts: Equinix's first AI-ready datacenter in India, opened September 2025 with USD 69 million investment. Connected to three Mumbai IBX facilities.

datacenters.name: NTT Chennai 1 — Ambattur
datacenters.cooling_type: Chilled Water with Variable Frequency Drives
datacenters.notable_facts: NTT's Chennai campus supports the second-highest submarine cable density in India after Mumbai.

datacenters.name: CtrlS Hyderabad DC — Rajendranagar
datacenters.cooling_type: Precision Cooling with Free Air Economizer
datacenters.notable_facts: Asia's first Tier IV certified datacenter. CtrlS signed MoU with Telangana government for 400 MW expansion at Chandan Valley.

datacenters.name: NTT Bengaluru 4 — Whitefield
datacenters.cooling_type: Liquid Cooling + Chilled Water — AI/HPC Ready
datacenters.notable_facts: NTT's 4th Bengaluru campus spanning 8.5 acres with INR 2,400 crore investment. Phase 4A (22.4 MW) already operational.

datacenters.name: Nxtra by Airtel — Manesar
datacenters.notable_facts: Part of Nxtra's 14-datacenter India portfolio with 200 MW total capacity. Bharti Airtel investing $600 million in expansion.

datacenters.name: Equinix SG1 — One-North
datacenters.notable_facts: Most network-dense carrier-neutral datacenter in Southeast Asia. Home to one of three global GRX peering points. Part of Equinix's 5-facility Singapore campus.

datacenters.name: Digital Realty SIN10 — Loyang
datacenters.notable_facts: Multi-story 50 MW facility with 100% renewable energy coverage through direct retail energy agreements. Part of PlatformDIGITAL ecosystem.

datacenters.name: STT GDC Singapore 6 — Tai Seng
datacenters.notable_facts: Singapore's first NVIDIA DGX Ready certified datacenter (2025). Features liquid cooling for dense AI deployments and GPU-as-a-Service capabilities.

datacenters.name: AirTrunk SGP1 — Loyang
datacenters.notable_facts: AirTrunk secured SGD 2.3 billion green loan in 2025 for SGP2 expansion targeting 70+ MW AI-powered capacity.

datacenters.name: Keppel DC Singapore 4 — Gul Circle
datacenters.notable_facts: Part of Keppel DC REIT portfolio — one of Asia's few pure-play datacenter REITs listed on SGX.

datacenters.name: Digital Realty DUB10 — Profile Park
datacenters.cooling_type: Free Air Cooling — Temperate Climate Optimized
datacenters.notable_facts: Digital Realty is Ireland's largest operator. Dublin has the third-largest datacenter market in Europe at 738 MW, behind only London and Amsterdam.

datacenters.name: Equinix DB3 — Blanchardstown
datacenters.notable_facts: Located in Dublin's key interconnection zone. Ireland's data centers consume 21% of national electricity — Dublin has paused new builds until 2028.

datacenters.name: Echelon Data Centres DUB20 — Clondalkin
datacenters.notable_facts: Echelon is one of Ireland's largest upcoming capacity contributors. Uses zero mechanical cooling — industry-leading PUE of 1.20.

datacenters.name: EdgeConneX — Cork
datacenters.notable_facts: Cork diversifies Ireland's datacenter geography beyond Dublin. Benefits from proximity to Apple's European HQ and pharma manufacturing corridor.

datacenters.name: Equinix LD5 — Slough Campus
datacenters.cooling_type: Chilled Water with Free Cooling Economizer
datacenters.notable_facts: Part of Equinix's Slough campus (LD4/5/6/10) with 67 MW combined. Slough is the UK's second-largest datacenter hub after London proper. UK is Equinix's second-biggest market globally.

datacenters.name: VIRTUS London INCEPTION — Hayes
datacenters.cooling_type: Indirect Evaporative Cooling with Adiabatic Assist
datacenters.notable_facts: VIRTUS has overtaken Equinix as the UK's largest datacenter operator by total capacity. Parent STT GDC reports 78% renewable energy across portfolio.

datacenters.name: Digital Realty LON1 — Sovereign House, Docklands
datacenters.notable_facts: Digital Realty expanded to 14 UK facilities after USD 200 million Slough acquisition in July 2024. Equinix, Digital Realty, and NTT control over 44% of London's installed MW.

datacenters.name: Kao Data MAN1 — Manchester
datacenters.notable_facts: Manchester is the UK's fastest-growing datacenter market outside London. Kao Data specializes in high-performance computing and AI workloads.

datacenters.name: Vantage Data Centres — Newport
datacenters.notable_facts: Newport is emerging as a key UK datacenter hub outside the Greater London area, benefiting from lower land costs and Welsh Government incentives.

datacenters.name: Equinix DC2 — Ashburn

submarine_cables: Virginia Beach Cable Landing Station access

datacenters.notable_facts: Critical interconnection point in the datacenter capital of the world. Northern Virginia has 665+ datacenters and 4,000 MW of power — up to 70% of global internet traffic transits Loudoun County daily.

datacenters.name: QTS Ashburn — Mega Data Center
datacenters.notable_facts: One of the largest single-campus datacenters in Northern Virginia. Blackstone-owned QTS is driving aggressive expansion to serve AI demand.

datacenters.name: AWS US-East-1 — Haymarket Campus
datacenters.cooling_type: Custom Evaporative + Liquid Cooling for AI Racks
datacenters.notable_facts: The original AWS US-East-1 region — the world's most-used cloud availability zone. AWS is investing $9 billion in Virginia for 2026 expansion.

datacenters.name: CyrusOne Dallas — Carrollton Campus
datacenters.notable_facts: Dallas is a major hub with nearly 200 datacenters. Texas ranks second in the US with 413 facilities and 2.9 GW capacity (plus 3.1 GW planned).

datacenters.name: Microsoft Azure South Central — San Antonio
datacenters.notable_facts: Microsoft is investing $40 billion in Texas AI datacenter infrastructure through 2027. San Antonio campus serves as a critical US government cloud hub.

datacenters.name: Switch SUPERNAP — Austin
datacenters.cooling_type: Patented Hot/Cold Aisle with Free Cooling
datacenters.notable_facts: Switch operates with industry-leading PUE of 1.18. Austin is rapidly growing as a tech and AI datacenter hub alongside Dallas.

datacenters.name: Equinix SV5 — Silicon Valley
datacenters.cooling_type: Chilled Water with Precision Air Handling
datacenters.notable_facts: Equinix is building SV12x — a USD 600 million JV with PGIM Real Estate for 28+ MW xScale capacity in Silicon Valley.

datacenters.name: Google Cloud — The Dalles, Oregon
datacenters.cooling_type: Custom Evaporative Cooling — Columbia River Water
datacenters.notable_facts: One of Google's earliest and largest datacenter campuses. Achieves industry-leading PUE of 1.10 using Columbia River for evaporative cooling. Google's US active IT capacity is 508 MW.

datacenters.name: Digital Realty CHI1 — Chicago
datacenters.cooling_type: Chilled Water with Lake Michigan Water Access
datacenters.notable_facts: Chicago is a critical financial datacenter hub. Digital Realty signed agreements for 130+ MW of hyperscale capacity across Chicago, Dallas, Phoenix, and Virginia.

datacenters.name: QTS Atlanta — Suwanee Mega Campus
datacenters.notable_facts: Atlanta/Georgia has gained significant momentum in datacenter supply. QTS Suwanee is one of the largest single-campus facilities in the Southeast US.

datacenters.name: AWS US-East-2 — Columbus Campus
datacenters.cooling_type: Evaporative Cooling with Liquid Cooling for AI Racks
datacenters.notable_facts: Ohio ranks third in US datacenter capacity at 1.6 GW with 2.4 GW planned. AWS invested $50 billion for over 1 GW of AI and supercomputing capacity for the US government.

datacenters.name: Global Switch Singapore — Tai Seng
datacenters.notable_facts: Global Switch's Tai Seng facility is a key carrier hotel in Southeast Asia. Strategic cooperation with TIME dotCom strengthens routes toward Indochina via Malaysia.

datacenters.name: GreenScale — Ennis Data Centre Campus
datacenters.notable_facts: GreenScale is a major contributor to Ireland's upcoming capacity. Ennis campus leverages Atlantic maritime climate for zero-mechanical-cooling operations with industry-leading PUE.

India.market_context: India's datacenter capacity reached 1.5 GW by end of 2025, with 387 MW added in 2025 alone (103% YoY growth). Projected to triple to 4 GW by 2030. Mumbai accounts for 52% of national capacity, Chennai at 21%.
India.regulatory_notes: Data localisation under DPDP Act 2023. Multiple state-level datacenter policies offering tax benefits and land subsidies.

Singapore.market_context: Total capacity exceeds 700 MW. Government-controlled expansion via Data Centre Call for Applications (CFA) framework after lifting 2022 moratorium. Market valued at USD 4.33 billion in 2025.
Singapore.regulatory_notes: CFA approval required for new capacity. Green Data Centre Roadmap mandates sub-1.2 PUE for new builds. SS 564 certification standard.

Ireland.market_context: 37 existing datacenters with 82 operational facilities total. Dublin has the third-largest market in Europe at 738 MW. Datacenters consume 21% of national electricity. Moratorium on new Dublin builds until 2028.
Ireland.regulatory_notes: Strict energy consumption limits. GDPR-compliant jurisdiction. Pause on new builds in Greater Dublin until 2028 due to grid constraints.

United Kingdom.market_context: 240+ existing datacenters. Total capacity at 1.7 GW with 3.5–4 GW upcoming. London dominates with 60% of upcoming capacity. VIRTUS leads as top UK operator, ahead of Equinix and Digital Realty.
United Kingdom.regulatory_notes: Growing energy scrutiny. Government designated datacenters as Critical National Infrastructure in 2024.

United States.market_context: 1,135+ existing colocation centers, 491 upcoming. Northern Virginia alone has 665 datacenters and ~4,000 MW. Texas second with 413 facilities and 2.9 GW. Combined hyperscaler capex (AWS, Microsoft, Google, Meta) was $228 billion in 2024, projected $320 billion in 2025.
United States.regulatory_notes: State-level incentives vary significantly. Virginia offers 6% sales tax exemption on datacenter equipment. Federal infrastructure investment acts driving expansion.
